title: Geography (India & World)
intro: Geography in SSC is map-and-fact recall: India's physical features, its rivers and mountains, the world's continents and oceans, and the basics of climate and agriculture. The trick is to attach each fact to a mental map — where the Western Ghats run, which river is the longest, which state grows what. This chapter organises the highest-frequency facts so you can revise the whole syllabus quickly and place every answer confidently.

topics.name: Physical Geography of India
topics.details: India has four broad physical divisions: the Himalayas in the north, the Indo-Gangetic plains, the Peninsular plateau (the Deccan), and the coastal plains with islands. Rajasthan is the largest state by area, and the Tropic of Cancer divides India almost in half.

topics.name: Rivers, Mountains & Lakes
topics.details: The Ganga is India's longest river. Peninsular rivers include the Godavari (longest in the south, the 'Dakshin Ganga'); the Narmada and Tapti are the two big rivers that flow WEST into the Arabian Sea.

topics.name: World Geography
topics.details: There are seven continents (Asia largest, Australia smallest) and five oceans (Pacific largest, Arctic smallest). The Equator (0° latitude) and the Prime Meridian (0° longitude, through Greenwich) are the two master reference lines.

topics.name: Climate & Agriculture
topics.details: India has a monsoon climate: the South-West Monsoon (June–September) brings most of the annual rainfall. Crops are grouped into Kharif (monsoon-sown), Rabi (winter) and Zaid (summer).

shortcuts: Attach every fact to a mental map of India and the world.
Ganga = longest in India; Godavari = longest peninsular (Dakshin Ganga).
Narmada & Tapti are the west-flowing exceptions (Arabian Sea).
Pacific = largest ocean; Asia = largest continent; Nile = longest river.
mistakes: Calling Everest "India's highest peak" — it is in Nepal; Kangchenjunga is highest within India.
Mixing up Kharif and Rabi crops.
Forgetting Narmada/Tapti flow west, not east.
Confusing largest freshwater lake (Wular) with largest lagoon (Chilika).
pyq: SSC asks river/mountain/soil facts, the monsoon and crop seasons for India, and continent/ocean/longest-river superlatives for the world. Map-anchored recall is the fastest route.
summary: Pin India's four physical divisions, its major rivers (Ganga longest; Narmada/Tapti west-flowing) and soils to a mental map, and learn the world superlatives (Pacific, Asia, Nile, Everest). Know the monsoon cycle and Kharif/Rabi/Zaid crops — these recur every paper.
